mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increase and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increase and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in real GDP by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals a contraction in economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 decline and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% month-over-month signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth expectations improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increase and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts over three consecutive months indicates a strengthening demand for housing, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the broader economy benefits from the housing market's strength.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of periods with sustained HOUST increase, or the correlation between sustained HOUST increase and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same month, it signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as economic growth expectations improve.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k & UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of PAYEMS increase and UNRATE decrease on positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it indicates inflationary pressure under a tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
regime_hint: inflationary pressure under tight monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and increasing CPIAUCSL on negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) grows by less than 1% quarter-over-quarter and retail and food services sales (RSAFS) decline by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals a weakening demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and economic growth slow.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 grows < 1% QoQ & RSAFS decreases > 1% MoM
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of low GDPC1 growth and declining RSAFS on negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
